defects.quote: most slow samples were inside workload-04 while earlier run phases appear much faster
defects.why: Whole-run and window percentile aggregates cannot establish where most slow samples occurred or characterize the non-window portion.

notes: Otherwise gives evidence-based, testable checks and preserves the FAIL verdict.

defects.quote: latency degradation appears concentrated in the trailing 300 s evaluation window
defects.why: The overall and evaluation-window aggregates cover different windows and cannot locate the concentration or onset of slow samples.

notes: It accurately reports the verdicts, validity, coverage, and key measurements apart from the unsupported aggregate-to-window inference.

defects.quote: high-latency samples appear concentrated inside the evaluation window
defects.why: The distinct whole-run and evaluation-window percentile aggregates cannot establish where high-latency samples were concentrated.

defects.quote: the cluster of max latency near 30050 ms
defects.why: The evidence gives only a maximum latency and provides no count showing a cluster of samples at or near that value.

notes: The core verdict reporting and most recommended checks are sound, but the unsupported aggregate inferences could mislead investigation.

defects.quote: Requests completed without recorded errors and at the target send rate, so the latency failure appears tied to time-to-completion rather than to dropped, failed, or under-sent traffic.
defects.why: Zero recorded JTL errors and matching aggregate rates do not rule out dropped requests, failures, or generator problems, nor establish that requests completed at the configured target rate.

defects.quote: error_count = 0 and throughput matched the 110 rps target, so the multi-second P95 is a processing / time-to-completion issue
defects.why: The evidence does not establish that the latency problem is necessarily a processing or completion-time issue rather than another unobserved failure mode.

notes: It includes several useful bounded checks, but overstates what zero recorded errors and aggregate throughput prove.
